questions.q: Why can't a GitHub Actions runner just use the profiles.yml from your own laptop?
options: A fresh runner has no home directory with your personal config files, so the workflow has to generate a profiles.yml itself, every run, from environment variables
profiles.yml is a Windows-only file format
GitHub Actions runners are not allowed to connect to databases under any circumstances
dbt does not support profiles.yml on any platform
questions.explain: A CI runner starts empty every time, so connection details have to come from environment variables read via env_var(...), not a pre-existing personal config file.

questions.q: What does dbt's env_var(...) function do inside profiles.yml?
options: Reads a value from an environment variable at run time, instead of hardcoding it as literal text
Permanently writes a secret into the repository
Deletes the profiles.yml file after use
Encrypts the entire dbt project
questions.explain: env_var(...) is dbt's built-in Jinja function for pulling a value from the environment at run time, keeping literal secrets out of the file.

questions.q: Why is dbt build generally the better choice for CI than running dbt run and dbt test as two separate commands?
options: dbt build runs models, tests, and seeds together in dependency order, stopping before building on top of data that already failed a test
dbt build is a purely cosmetic alias with no functional difference
dbt build skips all tests entirely, making CI runs faster
dbt build only works outside of CI environments
questions.explain: Running dbt run then dbt test as two commands would build every model regardless of upstream test failures; dbt build stops before building on top of already-broken data.

questions.q: What does a step-level env: block in a GitHub Actions workflow do?
options: Scopes those environment variables to that one step's process only
Makes those variables available to every future workflow in the repository forever
Deletes all other environment variables on the runner
Has no effect unless the job also defines on:
questions.explain: A step-level env: block injects variables only for that specific step's process, which is exactly what env_var(...) reads inside profiles.yml during that step.

questions.q: When a dbt test fails inside a CI run, what does the log actually show?
options: Exactly which test failed and how many rows violated it — the same output dbt prints locally, just captured by CI
A generic 'something went wrong' message with no further detail
Nothing — failed tests are silently ignored in CI by default
Only the name of the person who wrote the failing test
questions.explain: CI captures the same detailed test output dbt would print locally, including which test failed and the row count that violated it, and turns the step red on the PR.
